correctness.rationale: The standard greedy-arch theorem identifies subsequence universality U with the number of complete-alphabet greedy arches. Binary Thue–Morse t(8j+i)=t(j) xor t(i) and the explicit difference coding yield exactly four aligned length-16 templates according to (t(j),t(j+1)). Independently reconstructed these four templates; exhaustive scan of all four against all eight input masks finds exactly five completed arches, and every incoming singleton mask exits as the singleton of the last symbol. Thue–Morse cannot contain 000 or 111 (via even/odd recurrences); the remaining six adjacent triples and all first 0≤r<16 positions give floor(r/3) plus the single correction for k≥1,r=2,t(k−1)≠t(k). Thus U(16k+r)=5k+floor(r/3)+correction for every k, not only tested k. Independent direct difference-word scan confirmed the formula on 160001 prefixes; the finite-table reduction itself is the infinite argument. Remainder check gives -10≤16U(N)-5N≤6, sharp at r=2 for equal/unequal adjacent t; both occur infinitely using t(4j+1)=t(4j+2) and t(4j)≠t(4j+1).
residual_risks: The automatic source word is fixed by x(n)=1+t(n)-t(n+1) and prefix begins at n=0; contiguous factors, rotations and other ternary words are not covered.

value.rationale: Every-prefix coverage by arbitrary scattered subsequences is an established natural word-combinatorics invariant. The exact formula for a canonical ternary squarefree infinite word, global 5/16 density, sharp bounded discrepancy and a nontrivial single-residue correction form a motivated closed classification, not merely an arbitrary numerical prefix census.
residual_risks: No claim about contiguous factors, circular universality or arbitrary other morphic words.

final_claim: For ternary Thue–Morse difference word x(n)=1+t(n)-t(n+1), U(16k+r)=5k+floor(r/3)+1_{k≥1,r=2,t(k−1)≠t(k)}; density 5/16 and sharp discrepancy -10≤16U−5N≤6.
limitations: Applies only to ordinary scattered subsequences of zero-origin prefixes of the exact ternary difference word.
A previously unindexed same-word arch classification cannot be ruled out.
